items.content: I ask of life one simple courtesy: a fair fight. To which Life responds, LOL. In all caps. What a bitch.
items.translation: 我要求生活有一个简单的礼貌：公平的战斗。生活对此做出回应，哈哈。总而言之，真是个婊子。
items.author: GameCTRL

items.content: I ask of life to recognise my struggles and reward me not on my troubles.
items.translation: 我要求生活承认我的挣扎，而不是奖励我的烦恼。
items.author: Hummie Hunk

items.content: I ask of life these few things — be kind and play fair in whatever it brings!
items.translation: 我对生活有以下几点要求--无论带来什么，都要善待并公平对待！
items.author: Emily Keith

items.content: I ask of life that it move just a tad bit slower, for I'm not too anxious to get to the end.
items.translation: 我要求生活稍微慢一点，因为我不急于走到尽头。
items.author: Louis Koukoulas

items.content: I ask of life that it makes me love, that it makes me laugh, and that it makes me learn.
items.translation: 我对生活的要求是，它让我爱，它让我发笑，它让我学习。
items.author: Amanda Foote

items.content: I ask of life to surround me with love, and never let me lose sight of what's really important.
items.translation: 我要求生命用爱包围我，从不让我忘记真正重要的事情。
items.author: Amelia Bedilia

items.content: I ask of life to breathe goodness and all of its self into me so that my being may truly live instead of just existing.
items.translation: 我要求生命将善良及其全部自我注入我，以便我的存在可以真正活着，而不仅仅是存在。
items.author: J'

items.content: I ask of life... but it doesn't always give me what I ask for, so I've stopped asking and started enjoying.
items.translation: 我问生活......但它并不总是给我我所要求的，所以我已经停止了问，并开始享受。
items.author: Annelize Botha

items.content: The wings of hope soar on drifts of ambition.
items.translation: 希望的翅膀在雄心壮志的飘荡中翱翔。
items.author: John Ohlms

items.content: The wings of angels and devils are in all of us. Realize which wings are useful to you.
items.translation: 天使和魔鬼的翅膀在我们所有人身上。意识到哪些翅膀对您有用。
items.author: Jakarat Chotdamorng

items.content: The wings of one's greatest glory unfold when the heart and body are uninhibited.
items.translation: 当心灵和身体不受约束时，一个人最大的荣耀的翅膀就会展开。
items.author: Danette Johnson

items.content: The wings of forgiveness will carry you away from any disaster.
items.translation: 宽恕的翅膀将带你远离任何灾难。
items.author: Khristafer

items.content: The wings of love escort us to happiness and shield us from pain!
items.translation: 爱的翅膀护送我们走向幸福，保护我们免受痛苦！
items.author: Kelli Ross-Hall

items.content: Gratitude is not an expression. It is the language of respect, relief, and honor.
items.translation: 感恩不是一种表达方式。它是尊重、宽慰和荣誉的语言。
items.author: Mikhael Dominico

items.content: Gratitude is how nature intended us to feel, belong and give back.
items.translation: 感恩是大自然希望我们感受、归属和回馈的方式。
items.author: Lakshmi Gandhi

items.content: Gratitude is the gift of being humble and awed.
items.translation: 感恩是谦逊和敬畏的礼物。
items.author: Anna Page

items.content: Gratitude: staying humble when fate smiles on you.
items.translation: 感恩：当命运对你微笑时，保持谦虚。
items.author: Quintus Nienaber

items.content: I made these poems— these fugitive, these few— because I had to, and because of you. Because of you and song I came to make them. They are all yours, Euterpe. Will you take them?
items.translation: 我写了这些诗--这些逃亡的诗，这些诗--是因为我不得不写，也是因为你。因为你和歌，我来制作它们。它们都是你的，尤特佩斯。你会带走他们吗？
items.author: Humbert Wolfe

items.content: Dedicated to my dear wife who daily lives a far more beautiful poem than I can ever hope to write.
items.translation: 献给我亲爱的妻子，她每天都生活在一首比我希望写的更美丽的诗中。
items.author: Amos R. Wells

items.content: To DR. AND MRS. JOHN T. HARRINGTON Life flings miles and years between us, It is true,— But brings never to me dearer Friends than you!
items.translation: 对于JOHN T. HARRINGTON博士和夫人来说，生命在我们之间飘荡了数英里和数年，这是真的—但从来没有给我带来比你更亲爱的朋友！
items.author: Dorothy Scarborough

items.content: To the men and women who wrote this book, and speak to us here and now, of things without time; and those who speak to us, here and now, from beyond the stars
items.translation: 写这本书的男人和女人，在这里和现在对我们说话，谈论没有时间的事情；以及那些在这里和现在从星星之外和我们说话的人
items.author: John K. Terres

items.content: To mom and dad, for filling my head with endless dreams, my hands with endless books, and my heart with endless love.
items.translation: 致父母，让我的头脑充满无尽的梦想，我的双手充满无尽的书籍，我的心充满无尽的爱。
items.author: Kelseyleigh Reber

items.content: I dedicate this novel to my father, J OACHIM A LBERT W OLFGANG G EORGE , known as Broad Jo... Papa, you were the only person who read everything I ever wrote from the moment I learned to write. I will miss you at all times. I see you in every ray of evening light and in every wave of every sea. You left in midsentence.
items.translation: 我把这本小说献给我的父亲， J OACHIM A LBERT W OLFGANG G EORGE ，被称为Broad Jo... Papa ，你是唯一一个从我学会写作的那一刻起就阅读我所写的一切的人。我会时刻想念您。我在每一道傍晚的光芒中，在每一片大海的每一波浪潮中，都能看到你。您是中途离开的。
items.author: Nina George

items.content: Also, if you find holes in my book that you could drive a car through, do not be too sure they were not left there for that express purpose.
items.translation: 此外，如果您在我的书中发现可以开车通过的漏洞，请不要太确定它们不是为了明确的目的而留在那里的。
items.author: Mary Hunter Austin

items.content: To Phillpotts "Minor" as a trifling tribute of fraternal regard and in green and grateful memory of our boyhood
items.translation: 献给Phillpotts “未成年人” ，这是对我们兄弟般关怀的微不足道的敬意，也是对我们童年的绿色和感恩的回忆
items.author: Eden Phillpotts

items.content: The publishers wish me to stand in the vestibule of this book and open the door for the people. Those who enter these portals will find three rooms grandly furnished, a picture-gallery, a music-hall, and a library.
items.translation: 出版商希望我站在这本书的前厅，为人民敞开大门。进入这些门户的人会发现三个房间布置华丽，一个画廊，一个音乐厅和一个图书馆。
items.author: T. De Witt Talmage

items.content: Dedicated to All Who Still Have the Natural Child Love for Rhyme and Verse
items.translation: 献给所有仍然对韵律和诗歌有着天然孩子爱心的人
items.author: Elon Allan Richards

items.content: This book is published by the author. Brickbats, bouquets and orders — all equally welcome — may be addressed to: J. W. Cunningham, Robinwood Ave, Toledo 10, O.
items.translation: 本书由作者出版。砖蝙蝠、花束和订单—同样欢迎—可发送至： J. W. Cunningham, Robinwood Ave, Toledo 10, O.
items.author: J. W. Cunningham

items.content: To J OSEPH C ONRAD A Novelist Who Understands as Poets Do
items.translation: 致J OSEPH C ONRAD一位像诗人一样理解的小说家
items.author: Christopher Morley

items.content: To all those who struggle to care for aging parents, may God grant you love and grace beyond your wildest dreams...
items.translation: 对于所有努力照顾年迈父母的人，愿上帝赐予你超越你最疯狂梦想的爱和恩典......
items.author: Lauraine Snelling

items.content: This is a bawdy tale. Herein you will find gratuitous shagging, murder, spanking, maiming, treason, and heretofore unexplored heights of vulgarity and profanity, as well as non-traditional grammar, split infinitives, and the odd wank. If that sort of thing bothers you, then gentle reader pass by, for we endeavor only to entertain, not to offend.
items.translation: 这是一个卑鄙的故事。在这里，你会发现无端的shagging ，谋杀，打屁股，致残，叛国，以及迄今为止未被探索的粗俗和亵渎的高度，以及非传统的语法，分裂的无穷大和奇怪的wank。如果这种事情困扰着你，那么温柔的读者会路过，因为我们只努力娱乐，而不是冒犯。
items.author: Christopher Moore

items.content: Under every full moon there's a star within your reach making your impossible dreams come true.
items.translation: 在每个满月下，都有一颗恒星在你的触手可及的范围内，让你不可能的梦想成真。
items.author: @Joey_T

items.content: THIS BOOK, NOT BEING A CYNICAL NOVEL, FOR THE BLASÉS OF SOCIETY, NOR A GOOD-NATURED STORY, ABOUNDING IN SLANG AND VULGARITY, FOR THE YOUTHFUL READER, NOR THE PRODUCTION OF ONE WHO HAS SOUGHT THE ACQUAINTANCE OF CRITICS, WITH THE VIEW OF PURCHASING OR CONCILIATING THEIR GOOD OPINION, IS DEDICATED TO THE MASTER SPIRIT OF THE AGE, THE GREAT POOH! POOH! WITH THE HUMBLE CERTAINTY OF HIS FAVOURABLE JUDGMENT.
items.translation: 这本书不是一本愤世嫉俗的小说，也不是一个善意的故事，充斥着俚语和庸俗，对于年轻的读者，也不是一个为了购买或调解他们的好意见而寻求评论家认识的人的作品，它致力于这个时代的主人精神，伟大的维尼！维尼！以他谦卑的判断力。
items.author: Charles Mackay

items.content: To My Dear Friend CLAIRE DANA MUMFORD but for whose genius for appreciation this book would still be a bundle of dusty notes in my files.
items.translation: 致我亲爱的朋友克莱尔·达纳·芒福德（ CLAIRE DANA MUMFORD ） ，但对于他欣赏的天才来说，这本书仍然是我档案中一捆尘土飞扬的笔记。
items.author: Mary Hunter Austin

items.content: Dedicated TO THE SOFT SPOT IN THE WORLD'S GREAT HEART
items.translation: 致力于世界伟大心灵的柔软点
items.author: Charles F. Raymond

items.content: PREFACE . Yours Truly, F ANNY F ERN .
items.translation: 前言。您真诚的， F ANNY F ERN。
items.author: Folly As It Flies

items.content: TO BIG-HEARTED, BIG-SOULED, BIG-BODIED FRIEND CONAN DOYLE
items.translation: 致大心肠、大灵魂、大血统的朋友柯南·道尔
items.author: Jerome K. Jerome

items.content: FOR BARBARA With whom I listen to the birds, name the wild flowers, and count the stars.
items.translation: 对于我倾听鸟儿声音的芭芭拉，请为野花命名，并数数星星。
items.author: Hal Borland

items.content: For Barbara, especially in Autumn I gave you emeralds in May and amethysts in June; July I gave you turquoise skies and silver stars and moon. December will bring Diamonds, but before the frosty cold I give you coal-hot rubies and October's molten gold.
items.translation: 为了芭芭拉，特别是在秋天，我在五月给你祖母绿，六月给你紫水晶；七月，我给你绿松石般的天空、银色的星星和月亮。12月将带来钻石，但在寒冷的寒冷之前，我给你煤热的红宝石和10月的熔金。
items.author: Hal Borland

items.content: TO THE MEMORY OF THE LAST GREAT LIBERATOR OF THE HUMAN SPIRIT WILLIAM JAMES
items.translation: 纪念最后一位伟大的人类精神解放者威廉·詹姆斯
items.author: F. C. S. Schiller

items.content: Gentle Reader, — It is customary to omit prefaces. I beg you to make an exception in my particular case; I have something I really want to say.
items.translation: Gentle Reader ， —通常省略前言。我恳求你在我的特殊情况下破例；我有一些我真正想说的话。
items.author: Harriet Beecher Stowe

items.content: F OR MY VISITOR TO A ROOM ON N O. 10 S TAIRCASE AT W ADHAM C OLLEGE, AND BECAUSE OF EVERYTHING
items.translation: F或我的访客入住位于W ADHAM C OLLEGE的N O. 10 S TAIRCASE的房间，因为
items.author: Humbert Wolfe

items.content: T O T HOSE W HO H ATE THE P OWERS OF D ARKNESS
items.translation: T O T软管W HO H ATE THE P OWERS OF D ARKNESS
items.author: Adolf Wolff

items.content: Dedicated for no obvious reason to the Master of Lovat
items.translation: 无缘无故献给洛瓦特大师
items.author: Ronald A. Knox

items.content: APPENDIX. (This part of the book may be cut out.)
items.translation: 附录。（本书的这一部分可能会被剪掉。）
items.author: Noah Lott

items.content: FINIS. Now these lines that I have penn'd Some idle hours to spend, 'Tis too late to mend, Tho' some offend. Luck attend You, friend. END.
items.translation: FINIS.现在这些我已经花费了一些闲置时间的台词， '太晚了，无法修复， Tho'有些冒犯。祝你好运，朋友。结束。
items.author: Exul (Richard Le Gallienne

items.content: “T HESE and other sketches, with which... my Journal was copiously filled, were intended for the side scenes and backgrounds and exterior adornment of a work of fiction, of which the plan had imperfectly developed itself in my mind...”
items.translation: “这些草图和其他草图……我的日记里充满了各种各样的素描，这些草图是为了一部小说作品的场景、背景和外观装饰而设计的，而在我的脑海中，这个计划并没有得到完美的发展……”
items.author: Nathaniel Hawthorne

items.content: Under every full moon lies a reflection of the stars, and under every star lies a reflection of someone's soul.
items.translation: 每个满月下都有星星的倒影，每个星星下都有人灵魂的倒影。
items.author: Ruthie Fer Shure

items.content: Under every full moon the wine is sweeter and never runs dry.
items.translation: 在每个满月下，葡萄酒都更甜，永远不会干涸。
items.author: J. Darren Hicks

items.content: Under every full moon love brays, love frays, and in the end love obeys.
items.translation: 在每个满月下，爱情的眼泪，爱情的泪水，最终爱情服从。
items.author: Lise

items.content: Under every full moon, there's light that brings joy to us during night.
items.translation: 在每个满月下，夜晚都有光给我们带来欢乐。
items.author: @Lauren Shea

items.content: Under every full moon sits a wishing child.
items.translation: 每个满月下都有一个许愿的孩子。
items.author: Nicole Patrick

items.content: Under every full moon, our hopes and dreams travel its beams.
items.translation: 在每次满月下，我们的希望和梦想都会随之而来。
items.author: Dorian

items.content: Give me a life of action, and I will accept its sorrow and its tragedy, if I may escape the way of inanition.
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: The first requirement in taking a step in the right direction is to take a step in some direction.
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: I have always thought the actions of men the best interpreters of their thoughts.
items.author: John Locke

items.content: Blind action is more dangerous than no action at all.
items.author: David Starr Jordan

items.content: Well done is better than well said.
items.author: Benjamin Franklin

items.content: Between saying and doing many a pair of shoes is worn out.
items.author: Italian proverb

items.content: It may be folly to expect adults to do what they may reasonably be expected to do, and as everyone should know, when everything has been said and done, more will have been said than done...
items.author: Ashley Montagu

items.content: Every man is the son of his actions.
items.author: Spanish proverb

items.content: The great man is the man who has the courage to act.
items.author: Martin H. Fischer

items.content: The shortest answer is doing.
items.author: Jacula Prudentum

items.content: The shortest answer is doing the thing.
items.author: "Detached Sentences

items.content: I have observed in my lifetime three levels of virtuous person — the person of virtuous action, the person of virtuous intention and the person of virtuous regret.
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: Action battles doubt.
items.author: Terri Guillemets

items.content: I will hasten to answer the cry of my soul, lest long unheeded it cease to call. I will speed me about my high endeavor, lest long delayed the fire burn low. I will quicken the day of the manifest, lest long unfilled I lose faith in my dreams.
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: The challenge of every day is to establish some relationship between what you want from life and your Daily Planner.
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: Never confuse movement with action.
items.author: Ernest Hemingway

items.content: Action is eloquence...
items.author: William Shakespeare

items.content: Many Buddhist practitioners recite the Five Remembrances daily. The fifth is, "My actions are my only true belongings. I cannot escape the consequences of my actions. My actions are the ground on which I stand."
items.author: Thich Nhat Hanh

items.content: Up and at it! Sleepyheads! Better wear our Shoes than Beds.
items.author: Arthur Guiterman

items.content: Note to self: finding a cool quote and writing it in your journal is not a substitute for Getting. It. Done.
items.author: Betsy Cañas Garmon

items.content: There's something real satisfying about working, and having gotten it done.
items.author: Lady Bird Johnson

items.content: Think wisely, weighing Word and Fact, But never Think too much to Act.
items.author: Arthur Guiterman

items.content: Action, indeed... is the last resource of those who know not how to dream.
items.author: Oscar Wilde

items.content: Between what you can and what you do lies a sea, and in its depths lies buried the wrecked will.
items.author: Marie Dubsky

items.content: One has to do things, since one cannot always be Boswell observant. Also one must live oneself.
items.author: H. G. Wells

items.content: The ratio of dreaming to doing varies inversely with the rate of accomplishment.
items.author: Dr. Idel Dreimer

items.content: There may be no very close relationship between fate and furniture, yet it is doubtful if any of the world's great problems have been solved by men sitting in easy rocking-chairs.
items.author: "Poor Richard Junior's Philosophy

items.content: Words are sometimes efficacious, but the best sermons have been preached by Example.
items.author: "Poor Richard Junior's Philosophy

items.content: There should be no disagreement between our lives and our doctrines.
items.author: Publilius Syrus

items.content: The greatest difficulty in attempting to remove a difficulty, is in thinking too much about the difficulty of removing the difficulty.
items.author: James Lendall Basford

items.content: An orator's life is more convincing than his eloquence.
items.author: Publilius Syrus

items.content: Never act until you have clearly answered the question: "What happens if I do nothing?"
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: The first step binds one to the second.
items.author: French proverb

items.content: And is then example nothing? It is everything. Example is the school of mankind, and they will learn at no other.
items.author: Edmund Burke

items.content: Not all my day can I spend in listening, for I, too, must evolve, ere the night comes on.
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: One Hour of Gallant Striving up the Hill Is worth a Hundred Years of Standing Still.
items.author: Arthur Guiterman

items.content: I do not believe in a fate that falls on men however they act; but I do believe in a fate that falls on them unless they act.
items.author: G.K. Chesterton

items.content: Action is the antidote to despair. Almost any kind of action, especially that which is intelligently planned, is better than spending one's days in a dither.
items.author: Cid Ricketts Sumner

items.content: The best remedy for hurt feelings is not complaint, but accomplishment.
items.author: Dr. Idel Dreimer

items.content: From the personals: "Bundle of good intentions seeks mind reader."
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: Doing things is not the same as getting things done.
items.author: Jared Silver

items.content: The trick to getting things done is to list things to do in doable order.
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: ...creative spirits always anticipate the course of events. They do not wait for the dawn of a new era. They resolutely begin the new era at the moment when they see that the old era is ended.
items.author: Samuel McChord Crothers

items.content: Hatred of evil should constrain you to right, not fear.
items.author: Publilius Syrus

items.content: A man can fool you with his mind, and his Soul and his Heart, but if you follow his feet you will pretty near find out where he is going.
items.author: Will Rogers

items.content: Let me do Something; this I chiefly ask; For doing Nothing is the Harder Task.
items.author: Arthur Guiterman

items.content: A man never catches up with his good intentions for to-morrow .
items.author: "Poor Richard Junior's Philosophy

items.content: The surest way to escape anxiety and defeat despair is action. Do, don't dwell.
items.author: Michael Josephson

items.content: The excitement of action conquers fear. But suspense is horrible.
items.author: "A Night Never To Be Forgotten

items.content: Doing nothing is harmless, but being busy doing nothing is not.
items.author: Eric Hoffer

items.content: It is a golden rule that one should never judge men by their opinions, but rather by what these opinions lead them to be.
items.author: Georg Christoph Lichtenberg

items.content: We all know them — the unstructured person whose every action seems aimless and the totally organized person whose every action defeats some purpose.
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: Prayers plow not! Praises reap not!
items.author: William Blake

items.content: Practical prayer is harder on the soles of your shoes than on the knees of your trousers.
items.author: Austin O'Malley

items.content: A nod, a bow, and a tip of the lid to the person who coulda and shoulda and did.
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: What ought to have been done, and what shall be done, often stifle doing between them.
items.author: Augustus William Hare and Julius Charles Hare

items.content: It is a sad lament — the happiness you might have found if you had taken the path that still lies right there in front of you.
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: They are little to be feared whose tongues are their swords.
items.author: Proverb

items.content: The problem is to be faced and the solution to be shirked.
items.author: Bernard Shaw

items.content: He that waits upon Fortune, is never sure of a Dinner.
items.author: Benjamin Franklin

items.content: If I set for myself a task, be it so trifling, I shall see it through. How else shall I have confidence in myself to do important things?
items.author: George S. Clason

items.content: Our Yankee trade... saves itself by its activity... in skating over thin ice, our safety is in our speed.
items.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

items.content: If life is not an adventure it's a sad venture, and drear at the price. After all life is after all; it is not what you make it, but what it makes you.
items.author: Kenneth Alfred Evelyn Alexander

items.content: Try, above all things to be still and to contain yourself. You always want to rush into action. Realise that a certain kind of stillness is the most perfect form of action, like a seed can wait. One's action ought to come out of an achieved stillness: not be a mere rushing on.
items.author: D.H. Lawrence

items.content: Action! — that one stupendous word I will translate into my soul. My days shall be peopled. There shall be runnings to and fro, and chatterings. There shall be pistons sounding, and the whirr of wheels. There shall be busy days' endings, with reckonings and summings-up.
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: Now and then it's good to list all the things you regularly do for which there was once a good reason.
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: I believe half the unhappiness in life comes from people being afraid to go straight at things.
items.author: William J. Locke

items.content: We can't do everything at once; but we can do something at once, can we not?
items.author: Asenath Carver Coolidge

items.content: When it seems that something can't be done, start it, and see if the rest of it can be done.
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: So that was the beginning of our big adventure. Before so very long we had Alice in Wonderland tearing her hair from jealousy.
items.author: Percy Keese Fitzhugh

items.content: ...he retained to his last hour his taste for the adventurous, the singular, and the uncommon, and never was steady enough to pursue perseveringly the drudgery of life.
items.author: The O'Hara Family

items.content: And the strongest emotion was that life was as precious as it was puzzling. It was an ecstacy because it was an adventure; it was an adventure because it was an opportunity.
items.author: G. K. Chesterton

items.content: Adventures are things that happen that aren't supposed to happen.
items.author: Percy Keese Fitzhugh

items.content: Well; keep good quarter and good care to-night: The day shall not be up so soon as I, To try the fair adventure of to-morrow.
items.author: William Shakespeare

items.content: Perhaps the greatest adventure in life is that period between the ignorance of knowledge and the knowledge of ignorance, called Middle Age.
items.author: Kenneth Alfred Evelyn Alexander

items.content: To pitch my tent with no prosy plan, To range and to change at will; To mock at the mastership of man, To seek Adventure's thrill.
items.author: Robert W. Service

items.content: Adventure stands at every cross-road and only the dun-grey kind with the one-way mind ignore him. But the variety-artist knows what his nose knows and goes where his nose goes, for it's hinged, although apparently unhinged, and if it leads him into trouble it also teaches him the scent of it.
items.author: Kenneth Alfred Evelyn Alexander

items.content: It is only in adventure that some people succeed in knowing themselves ŌĆö in finding themselves.
items.author: Andr├® Gide

items.content: Life is either a daring adventure or nothing.
items.author: Helen Keller

items.content: But what civilization was not founded on adventure, and how long could one exist without it? What justifies the risk of life? Some answer, the attainment of knowledge. Some say wealth, or power, is sufficient cause. I believe the risks are justified by the sheer love of the life I lead.
items.author: Charles Lindbergh

items.content: The traveler was active; he went strenuously in search of people, of adventure, of experience. The tourist is passive; he expects interesting things to happen to him. He goes "sight-seeing"...
items.author: Daniel J. Boorstin

items.content: Every production of an artist should be the expression of an adventure of his soul.
items.author: W. Somerset Maugham

items.content: Now nothing happened the next week except going to school, and gee whiz, there's no adventure in that.
items.author: Percy Keese Fitzhugh

items.content: In gardening, go lightly on caution, heavily on adventure, and see what comes out.
items.author: Ruth Stout

items.content: Without adventure civilization is in full decay.
items.author: Alfred North Whitehead

items.content: Equipped with his five senses, man explores the universe around him and calls the adventure Science.
items.author: Edwin Powell Hubble

items.content: The earth is sliced into furrows that seeds may burst with life; even thus with our wounds.
items.author: Henry Stanley Haskins

items.content: I forget just when, as a child reading fairy tales, I realized that you can "live happily ever after" after almost any gosh-darn thing.
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: I shall come, not as one who has escaped pain, but as one who has glorified it.
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: Yet this is what we must do if we want to make a real success of life. We must master the unpleasant, instead of letting the unpleasant master us.
items.author: H. Addington Bruce

items.content: The robb'd that smiles steals something from the thief...
items.author: William Shakespeare

items.content: Earth's tribulations diminish in proportion to the elevation of our souls.
items.author: James Lendall Basford

items.content: The best thing I know in favor of TIGHT SHOES is that it makes a fellow forget all of his other troubles.
items.author: Josh Billings

items.content: Pain is the great teacher of mankind. Beneath its breath souls develop.
items.author: Marie Dubsky

items.content: Bad is never good until worse happens.
items.author: Proverb

items.content: There's not a woe that is not sent to leave some good behind it, If only we would search it out, and trust until we find it... There's many cares to dog our steps, and many griefs distress us, But never yet a sorrow came that was not meant to bless us.
items.author: Lizzie Marshall Berry

items.content: My soul is like the oar that momently Dies in a desperate stress beneath the wave, Then glitters out again and sweeps the sea: Each second I'm new-born from some new grave.
items.author: Sidney Lanier

items.content: Life may take everything out of my days, but the real things remain. You may destroy my castles, but I have the timbers to build ten thousand more.
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: If, when most desperate, we examine our misery, we find it but a drop spattered from seas of trouble.
items.author: James Lendall Basford

items.content: Sometimes in tragedy we find our life's purpose — the eye sheds a tear to find its focus.
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: Not alone for that which is mine will I rejoice, but for that which has been withheld, which was coveted and longed for, but denied, for I am what I am for having had to rise superior to the need.
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: We carry our burden on and on, until one day, suddenly, we laugh and set it down upon the ground.
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: The smoothest path is no guarantee against a broken neck.
items.author: James Lendall Basford

items.content: Suffering is above, not below. And everyone thinks that suffering is below. And everyone wants to rise.
items.author: Antonio Porchia

items.content: The Lord gives us friends to push us to our potential — and enemies to push us beyond it.
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: ...the beauty of the world which is so soon to perish, has two edges, one of laughter, one of anguish, cutting the heart asunder.
items.author: Virginia Woolf

items.content: Fortune knocks but once at any man's door, but misfortune has much more patience.
Everybody wishes Miss Fortune would get married and settle down.
items.author: Detroit Journal

items.content: Adversity and failure are woven into the fabric of existence; without them, there can be neither test of mettle nor triumph of success.
items.author: Dr. Idel Dreimer

items.content: Don't mind a few bruises. Life's paths are full of stones and thorns. All are bound to hurt a little.
items.author: Minna Thomas Antrim

items.content: thorns and stings and those such things just make stronger our angel wings
items.author: Terri Guillemets

items.content: Half the annoyances of life will disappear if one is only patient under them. Almost all the other half will go the same way if one does not worry over them.
items.author: Frank A. De Puy

items.content: Sometimes I think my life would make a great TV movie. It even has the part where they say, "Stand by. We are experiencing temporary difficulties."
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: Endure the heavy burdens, and you will the more easily carry the lighter.
items.author: Publilius Syrus

items.content: Life may break my body and my days — and my soul may laugh at her impotency. She may destroy me, and I may go laughing over the hills. A few hours mutilated, and eternity lies in the residuum. She may mar the realities, but what of my dreams!
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: Yes, one must suffer, even in vain, so as not to have lived in vain.
items.author: Antonio Porchia

items.content: Life is light and shadow, and the light will come in its turn.
items.author: F. W. Robinson

items.content: When in sickness, age, or sorrow, Through great shadows we must move, Of all earthly lights the dearest Shines from hearts of those we love.
items.author: James Lendall Basford

items.content: Despair is anger with no place to go.
items.author: Mignon McLaughlin

items.content: Life is hard to bear. But do not pretend to be so frail! We are all good he-asses and she-asses of burden.
items.author: Friedrich Nietzsche

items.content: Again and again we cry "I can bear no more!" — that is the human of us. And again and again we bear more, — that is the god of us.
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: It's because so much happens. Too much happens. That's it. Man performs, engenders, so much more than he can or should have to bear. That's how he finds that he can bear anything. That's it. That's what is so terrible. That he can bear anything, anything.
items.author: William Faulkner

items.content: When I see a man who, bravely, Meets realities in life, Who carries on, courageously, In the face of grief and strife; Then, I bow my head in honour Of this man, with courage rare, Who has such strength of character, Who, bravely, his burdens bears!
items.author: Gertrude Tooley Buckingham

items.content: ...every struggle is a dance...
items.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

items.content: Notice the disappointing things and marvelous things at the same time, because they dance with one another.
items.author: Dr. SunWolf

items.content: The winds of misfortune always bring some seeds of opportunity.
items.author: William Arthur Ward

items.content: I guess if you take away the pain in life it means having no beauty to hope for.
items.author: Daniel

items.content: Adversity has the effect of eliciting talents which, in prosperous circumstances, would have lain dormant.
items.author: Horace

items.content: People are resilient. After all, every person born has recovered from nine months on life support.
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: But while to propose to be a better man is a piece of unscientific cant, to have become a deeper man is the privilege of those who have suffered. And such I think I have become.
items.author: Oscar Wilde

items.content: I am the strength that was born of my weakness. I am the steadfastness that came out of my wavering. I am the joy of living that was born of my despair. I am the poise that was born of my great unrest.
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: A new wound makes all the old ones ache again.
items.author: Mignon McLaughlin

items.content: Don't be an easy-doing child, do hard things too. Remember a blacksmith never got a big muscle by hammering an inch nail, but by swinging a heavy hammer while beating out an iron bar. Sometimes we must run hard roads, through briers, over sharp stones, and any which way.
items.author: Sunday School Helper

items.content: Even for wisdom it is a hard matter to bear affliction.
items.author: Publilius Syrus

items.content: It is the hard things that make men. It is hard things that bring mental discipline and mental muscle. It is what brings out manhood, to really conquer something.
items.author: Proceedings of the Dedication of the New Buildings of the Central High School

items.content: The sweetest pleasure arises from difficulties overcome.
items.author: Publilius Syrus

items.content: When life gives you lemons, please, just don't squirt them in other people's eyes.
items.author: J. Andrew Helt

items.content: The turning point in the process of growing up is when you discover the core of strength within you that survives all hurt.
items.author: Max Lerner

items.content: Had life been more abundant, I could not know the deep craving that comes from the sparsity of it. Had it been more verdant, I could not know the desert's pain.
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: Sooner or later, you will need to make friends with Disappointment.
items.author: Dr. SunWolf

items.content: Suffering... few people seem able to rouse themselves from their "soul sleep" without it.
items.author: Florence Scovel Shinn

items.content: It went in a Sorrow, but through the alchemy of Self, it came out a Song.
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: Invite your melancholy outside for a walk. Or read it a poem. Or bake it chocolate chip cookies.
items.author: Dr. SunWolf

items.content: Break bread with your darkness. Put down the stone in your fist. Write a poem on it, instead.
items.author: Dr. SunWolf

items.content: Lost dreams may help you find new dreams.
items.author: J Charles White

items.content: If we don't face and overcome unsettling events in life, we are ruled by them.
items.author: Bones

items.content: Pain is sometimes the cost of a meaningful existence. I can handle that.
items.author: Jeb Dickerson

items.content: At times, challenges hit with the force of a roaring, rushing waterfall. The true test, however, is whether you can put your arms up and enjoy the feel of the water.
items.author: Aviva Kaufman

items.content: Us to teach that love and grace In darkest days may blossom, And that a tender bloom of hope May shine in sorrow's bosom.
items.author: J. J. Britton

items.content: The rays of happiness, like those of light, are colorless when unbroken.
items.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow

items.content: I have been bent and broken, but — I hope — into a better shape.
items.author: Charles Dickens

items.content: The world breaks everyone, and afterward, some are strong at the broken places.
items.author: Ernest Hemingway

items.content: Bad times have a scientific value. These are occasions a good learner would not miss... We learn geology the morning after the earthquake, on ghastly diagrams of cloven mountains, upheaved plains, and the dry bed of the sea.
items.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

items.content: God uses suffering as a whetstone, to make men sharp with.
items.author: Henry Ward Beecher

items.content: The fact that life is a grind is what sharpens many a man's wits.
items.author: Boston Transcript

items.content: We shall draw from the heart of suffering itself the means of inspiration and survival.
items.author: Winston Churchill

items.content: Pour on; I will endure.
items.author: William Shakespeare

items.content: Who said a dilemma had only two horns? He must have been fooling around with little dilemmas before they were of age. A real dilemma has between eight and ten pairs of horns and can kill you as far as you can see it and vice versa.
items.author: Ernest Hemingway

items.content: DILEMMA Comes from dill , a pickle, and Emma , a person. A person in a pickle.
items.author: Charles Wayland Towne

items.content: ADVERSITY A bottomless lake, surrounded by near-sighted friends.
items.author: Charles Wayland Towne

items.content: The bitterest things are sweets misunderstood...
items.author: Mark Van Doren

items.content: How, after a run of ill-luck, of despair, life blossoms out unexpectedly.
items.author: William Gerhardi

items.content: [L]ook evil in the face; walk up to it, and you will find it less than you imagined, and often you will not find it at all; for it will recede as you advance.
items.author: Sydney Smith

items.content: Pigeons are people too.
items.author: Author unknown

items.content: Sometimes when Fortune scowls most spitefully, she is preparing her most dazzling gifts.
items.author: Winston Churchill

items.content: Men have made them gods of love, Sun-gods, givers of the rain, Deities of hill and grove: I have made a god of Pain. Of my god I know this much, And singing I repeat, Though there's anguish in his touch, Yet his soul within is sweet.
items.author: Æ

items.content: There are people who place a basket on your head to see what you carry.
items.author: Wolof proverb

items.content: We won't break, Mary. We look very small, but the reed can carry weight.
items.author: Emily Dickinson

items.content: What is to give light must endure burning.
items.author: Anton Wildgans

items.content: The truth is, we pamper little griefs into great ones, and bear great ones as well as we can.
items.author: William Hazlitt

items.content: A willing, working, soft-hearted, not hard-headed fellow, Plornish took his fortune as smoothly as could be expected; but it was a rough one.... he tumbled into all kinds of difficulties, and tumbled out of them; and, by tumbling through life, got himself considerably bruised.
items.author: Charles Dickens

items.content: Gold is tried by fire, fortitude by affliction.
items.author: Publilius Syrus

items.content: So do the Winds , and Thunders cleanse the Air: So working Seas settle and purge the Wine; So lop't and pruned Trees do flourish fair, So doth the Fire the drossy Gold refine.
items.author: John Davies

items.content: If the wind will not serve, take to the oars.
items.author: Proverb

items.content: Misfortune is a Wind that, rising higher, Blows out the Match but fans the Steady Fire.
items.author: Arthur Guiterman

items.content: When life takes the wind out of your sails, it is to test you at the oars.
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: When you forget to take the sail at all, then the wind is constantly in your favour both ways. But there! this world is only a probation, and man was born to trouble as the sparks fly upward.
items.author: Jerome K. Jerome

items.content: There is no seamanship on a smooth sea and in a fair wind. The storm is what makes the mariner.
items.author: William Ellis

items.content: Say not that this or that thing came to thwart you; it only came to test you.
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: Flowers never emit so sweet and strong a fragrance as before a storm. Beauteous soul! when a storm approaches thee, be as fragrant as a sweet-smelling flower.
items.author: Jean Paul Friedrich Richter

items.content: Small skill is gained by those who cling to Ease; The Able Sailor hails from Stormy Seas.
items.author: Arthur Guiterman

items.content: The gods give man one good, as an offset to two ills.
items.author: Publilius Syrus

items.content: Past and to come seems best; things present, worst.
items.author: William Shakespeare

items.content: The man who makes the best of opportunities is apt to get the best of obstacles.
items.author: "Poor Richard Junior's Philosophy

items.content: During the darkest indigo midnight, yet will countless stars blossom.
items.author: Dr. SunWolf

items.content: Difficulties need not be disastrous; defeats need not be fatal; failures need not be final.
items.author: William Arthur Ward

items.content: "O, woe is me T' have seen what I have seen, see what I..." Eh. Even Shakespeare never got this tragic.
items.author: The Middle

items.content: Fill our hearts rather with a noble discontent, the discontent that will cause us to move to better things.
items.author: Charles F. Raymond

items.content: Trouble will meet you half-way and will gladly accompany you the rest of the distance.
items.author: "Poor Richard Junior's Philosophy

items.content: To-day the heart feels fraught with woe, And keen-pronged thorns lie in the way, But as the Spring's breath melts the snow, E'en so our sorrows go, and gay And peaceful soars each troubled mind— Each sombre cloud is silver lined...
items.author: Kimball Chase Tapley

items.content: Your heart has been sore wounded too. Dear Light, love shall cherish you, till you again look on life with happy eyes.
items.author: Byron Caldwell Smith

items.content: I had this dream where I complained to the Lord that my life was not easy. "But did you not pray for happiness?" said the Lord. "Well, yes," I said. And the Lord said, "Well, make up your mind."
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: Human life is measured by pains and pleasures. Monotony sends us to sleep.
items.author: Thomas Clark Henley

items.content: No man ever understood the true meaning of life, or caught a glimpse of heaven, until repeated misfortunes had dispelled the flattering dream of a selfish imagination, and cured the blindness of his spiritual nature.
items.author: James Lendall Basford

items.content: Your enemies are the best reflection of your own character: a strong man rarely has weak foes.
items.author: "Poor Richard Junior's Philosophy

items.content: Smile like the rose whose petals are torn asunder— It says 'I gather beauty even from the thorn of grief.'
items.author: Rumi

items.content: ...for even our misfortunes are a part of our belongings...
items.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

items.content: It is the poor years that make the good ones so very good...
items.author: Edward Payson Powell

items.content: The secret of success chiefly lies in the determination to succeed and the resolve that every repulse, every knock-down he receives in the battle, will only nerve him the more.
items.author: Andrew Carnegie

items.content: Misfortunes never come singly because people always multiply them.
items.author: "Poor Richard Junior's Philosophy

items.content: The great doctors all got their education off dirt pavements and poverty — not marble floors and foundations.
items.author: Martin H. Fischer

items.content: A resolute spirit is not cast down by a single misfortune.
items.author: Publilius Syrus

items.content: "The horror of that moment," the King went on, "I shall never, never forget!" "You will, though," the Queen said, "if you don't make a memorandum of it."
items.author: Lewis Carroll

items.content: ...you are hugging your miseries close to you, and you will not let them go; and there is no other way for them to forsake you. Till you let them go, they cannot go. You are the one who must choose.
items.author: Ursula N. Gestefeld

items.content: ...and we take everything heartily and naturally in the right way, — for even mishaps are like knives, that either serve us or cut us, as we grasp them by the blade or the handle.
items.author: James Russell Lowell

items.content: When a man tries to drown troubles on his way home, he always finds them sitting and grinning on his doorstep like drenched cats.
items.author: "Poor Richard Junior's Philosophy

items.content: Each negative experience hardens us a little more to life. Some of us are tough as concrete. But try to leave yourself a few cracks, so that love and flowers can grow through.
items.author: Terri Guillemets

items.content: His fortune is shipwrecked...
items.author: Thomas Jefferson

items.content: When suffering comes, we yearn for some sign from God, forgetting we have just had one.
items.author: Mignon McLaughlin

items.content: Would you touch a nettle without being stung by it? take hold of it stoutly. Do the same to other annoyances, and hardly will any thing annoy you.
items.author: Augustus William Hare and Julius Charles Hare

items.content: Nothing grieves me more than when good character is locked up fast in the hardships of life.
items.author: Menander

items.content: I cursed my misfortune, — and it remained one.
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: Pain gives you the memory of things you shouldn't do.
items.author: Craig D. Slovak

items.content: There are tragedies in life that change us forever, the person we once were mistakenly listed among the survivors.
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: Some days, we're just looking for a soft place to land.
items.author: Dr. SunWolf

items.content: We paint our lives with passion and peace, with love and laughter — to cover the pain and scars, the bitterness and tears.
items.author: Terri Guillemets

items.content: I do not ask you to help me, but I would appreciate it if you did not hinder me.
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: Many a man can overcome a difficulty in the path of another, which he could not surmount were it in his own.
items.author: James Lendall Basford

items.content: I once read the sentence 'I lay awake all night with toothache, thinking about toothache and about lying awake.' That's true to life. Part of every misery is, so to speak, the misery's shadow or reflection...
items.author: N. W. Clerk

items.content: Can one deal with realities that are not shaken with sobs and wet with tears?
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: Adversity enhances this tale we call life.
items.author: Terri Guillemets

items.content: Come what come may, Time and the hour runs through the roughest day.
items.author: William Shakespeare

items.content: Like a plant that starts up in showers and sunshine and does not know which has best helped it to grow, it is difficult to say whether the hard things or the pleasant things did me most good.
items.author: Lucy Larcom

items.content: Life leaves its bootprints all over us — we just have to keep getting back up.
items.author: Terri Guillemets

items.content: In most cases, misfortune is an acquired habit.
items.author: James Lendall Basford

items.content: Even when life isn't good on the outside, you have an option to make it good from the inside out.
items.author: Terri Guillemets

items.content: The cold is a good counsellor, but it is cold.
items.author: Antonio Porchia

items.content: Eddie fell from grace with a thump. The town laughed at him, as people always laugh when a person — particularly so plump a person as Eddie was — falls hard on the slippery sidewalk of this icy world.
items.author: Rupert Hughes

items.content: I stood dazed... wondering... how Providence could let this happen to us. To us!
items.author: Stanley J. Weyman

items.content: In this world there are only two tragedies. One is not getting what one wants, and the other is getting it.
items.author: Oscar Wilde

items.content: Sir: there are two tragedies in life. One is not to get your heart's desire. The other is to get it.
items.author: Bernard Shaw

items.content: Difficulties are footholds toward maturity.
items.author: William Arthur Ward

items.content: Let me embrace thee, sour adversity, For wise men say it is the wisest course.
items.author: William Shakespeare

items.content: Sometimes, even as an optimist, you can have so much tragedy in your life that it gets really annoying.
items.author: Robert Brault

items.content: O God, whate'er befall, spare me that supreme calamity — let no after-bitterness settle down with me. Misfortune is not mine until that hour.
items.author: Muriel Strode

items.content: What are the best qualities in an advertisement writer? Optimism, cheerfulness, animal spirits, that give rainbow hues to commerce and poetic attributes to pills.
items.author: Arthur Brisbane

items.content: Doing business without advertising is like winking at a girl in the dark. You know what you are doing, but nobody else does.
items.author: Author unknown

items.content: ADVERTISE — The man who whispers down a well, About the goods he has to sell, Won't reap as many golden dollars As he who climbs a tree and hollers.
items.author: Josh Billings

items.content: No matter how great a business may be it must have a voice to tell what it is doing, and what it has to offer. The advertising man is the voice.
items.author: Arthur Brisbane

items.content: What is the difference between unethical and ethical advertising? Unethical advertising uses falsehoods to deceive the public; ethical advertising uses truth to deceive the public.
items.author: Vilhjalmur Stefansson

items.content: Many a small thing has been made large by the right kind of advertising.
items.author: Mark Twain

items.content: When a man throws an empty cigarette package from an automobile in California, he is liable to a fine of $50. When a man throws a billboard across a view, he is liable to be richly rewarded.
items.author: Edmund G. Brown

items.content: I think that I shall never see A billboard lovely as a tree. Indeed, unless the billboards fall I'll never see a tree at all.
items.author: Ogden Nash

items.content: And there is no question but that you can't sustain a mood, a dramatic mood of any particular kind, when at the end of the climactic moment of the scene, out come a couple of dancing rabbits with toilet paper.
items.author: Rod Serling

items.content: How can you put on a meaningful drama or documentary that is adult, incisive, probing, when every fifteen minutes the proceedings are interrupted by twelve dancing rabbits singing about toilet paper?
items.author: Rod Serling

items.content: The man who advertises a little and then says advertising does not pay is like unto the man who burns one match beneath a five-barrel kettle of water and then says fire will not heat water.
items.author: "Mental Hydrophobia

items.content: Advertisements are now and have been for some time recognized as an extremely important part of the industrial and business system of the United States.
items.author: Arthur Brisbane

items.content: Advertising may be described as the science of arresting the human intelligence long enough to get money from it. It is carried on by means of printed notices, signboards, placards and above all, owing to the simplicity of the human mind, by pictures.
items.author: Stephen Leacock

items.content: Advertising is multiplied information concerning the ability of the advertiser to supply a product or a service. It is news of the thing we wish to buy or the thing we may be influenced to buy. Advertising tells us where to secure that which will supply a need; often it actually creates the need.
items.author: Wilbur D. Nesbit

items.content: Advertising... will twist and adulterate any words it lays pen or tongue to for public consumption (free, meaning "if you buy something else"; instant, meaning "ten minutes of fast stirring"; optional, "it costs more"; giant economy size, meaning "spill what you save")...
items.author: Leonard Louis Levinson

items.content: You can tell the ideals of a nation by its advertisements.
items.author: Norman Douglas

items.content: Among the ads: A 20% price raise is a "slight advance" — but a 10% cut is "A DRASTIC REDUCTION!!"
items.author: J. W. Cunningham

items.content: Let advertisers spend the same amount of money improving their product that they do on advertising, and they wouldn't have to advertise.
items.author: Will Rogers

items.content: T ONY : Commercials are the cornerstone of a free market economy. J ONATHAN : And they give you time to go to the bathroom when you're watching TV. M ONA : Oh, that's why nobody watches public television.
items.author: Who's the Boss?

items.content: The public are swine; advertising is the rattling of a stick inside a swill-bucket.
items.author: George Orwell

items.content: Let the public discover that 5 per cent of your advertising is exaggeration, and it immediately suspects the other 95 per cent.
items.author: Walter E. Weld

items.content: Someone invented the automobile, And good Americans took the wheel To view American rivers and rills And justly famous forests and hills — But somebody equally enterprising Had invented billboard advertising...
items.author: Ogden Nash

items.content: Our leading advertisers have richly proved that the public will believe anything if they are told of it often enough.
items.author: Arnold Bennett

items.content: Moreover, the service of advertising is not confined to the world of trade. There are innumerable good causes which must ever depend upon the best and most skillful methods of publicity for their success and usefulness to mankind.
items.author: Frederick J. Allen

items.content: We don't know why we do it, but we do. Really and truly we don't need the money. And confidentially we are not overstocked. But we just can't help from marking things low. Look at our front window. You'll see things.
